messages:
alex: Customer (Acme Search) saw a string of 429s for ~2m during an hourly embed batch. They expected the smoothing/burst cushion to absorb it — but credits dropped to 0 quickly. Any idea what metric to check first?

maria: Thanks for flagging. Do we have their account id and the approximate start time?

alex: acct: acme-847; spike started at ~2026-03-15T14:22:00Z. They were doing concurrent embed requests (5 workers, each batching 64).

maria: got it. common cause: large concurrent batches can exhaust "ephemeral quota" faster because tokens are accounted when requests start not after completion.

devin: Confirming — our smoothing window tries to smooth per-minute consumption but if many requests hit simultaneously, the burst cushion can be consumed before the window evens out.

kevin: Two quick checks: 1) check account-level burst_credits metric in the billing dashboard for that timeframe, 2) check per-route concurrency in the trace for multiple inflight embed calls.

sam: Also look at the token accounting logs. For embedder jobs we count model_units at request time. If batches are larger than typical, you can get an instantaneous spike in the ledger. Example from logs: ```units_reserved=3200 concurrently_inflight=5 smoothing_window_ms=60000```

alex: ok running the queries now. What about config mitigations we can recommend to the customer ASAP?

maria: Short term: reduce per-worker batch size or add a small delay jitter between workers to spread starts across the smoothing window.

maria: Medium term: enable our adaptive_batching hint or pin them to a higher priority plan so they have larger cushion.

kevin: We can also suggest lowering concurrency to 2-3 while they backfill. If they need throughput, recommend ramping with a staged rollout (e.g., 10% -> 50% -> 100%) so smoothing gets time to adapt.

sam: From runtime side we can tweak smoothing_window_ms for the account (increase from default 60s to 120s) to make the window absorb short bursts better. That will increase perceived buffer but will slightly delay refill visibility.

alex: Would changing smoothing_window_ms require a deploy? Or is it a per-account flag?

devin: It's a per-account runtime config we can flip without redeploy. But must be toggled carefully — too large a window can mask real overuse.

quota-bot: [automated] acme-847 burst_credits at 2026-03-15T14:20:00Z -> 4200, 14:22:00Z -> 0, 14:24:00Z -> 0, 14:30:00Z -> 1800

maria: The bot output matches the timeline. They hit zero and then recovered slowly once the background refill kicked in.

alex: Customer also asked why their retries didn't succeed. They had immediate retries from app-level code.

kevin: Immediate retries often exacerbate the drain because they spawn more concurrent starts. Recommend exponential backoff with jitter; also honor 429 Retry-After if present.

sam: If they want a more resilient approach, we can suggest using client-side request queuing with congestion control: hold requests locally and release at a rate matching the smoothing refill.

alex: Ok I'll send customer an action plan: reduce batch size to 32, throttle workers to 2 concurrency, add jitter and exponential backoff, and offer us to flip smoothing_window_ms to 120s for a trial. Anything to add?

maria: Ask them to provide a short HAR or snippet of request start timestamps if they can reproduce; that helps us correlate ledger events.

kevin: From our side I'll open a short-lived account flag to increase smoothing and monitor metrics for 24h. If we see unexpected side effects we'll roll back.

devin: Also I'll add a quick dashboard tile for acme-847 showing live 'units_reserved' vs 'burst_credits' so support + SRE can watch the trial.

alex: Thanks all. I'll message the customer with the plan and ask for request-start timestamps. Will loop back. :thumbsup:
